drain.allocatorReleasePolicy: No malloc_zone_pressure_relief, madvise-style purge, or other allocator release request is made; the drain measures the live process unaided.

processSampling.handleCountMethod: PowerShell Get-Process HandleCount (Windows OS handle count)
processSampling.handleThreadSlackCalibrationNote: handleSlack and threadSlack were calibrated against Windows runtime/OS jitter for these counters.
processSampling.threadCountMethod: PowerShell Get-Process Threads.Count (Windows process thread count)

workloadWorkingSet.interpretation: The RSS trend's precondition. Opening a workspace builds a manifest of every captured entry, so the LIVE WORKING SET -- user files -- is what makes the process larger; the old workload grew it by 25 files per storm cycle past 57,000 files. Each scenario now rotates through identityRing identities and contentVariants payloads, so request volume is undiminished while the working set stays bounded. Growth beyond maxUserFileGrowth means the trend fit measured a growing workload and the RSS fields are reported as null rather than as a result. This bounds what drives RSS; it makes no claim about durable byte growth, which is append-only by design and tracked separately for the postCutoverContinuous tier.
